subject: tu:game/game/gamemain
value:
PHASE 3 investigation of work_claim.split-map-correction.20260904.v1 ('default_options @0x800520CC = GAMEDEFS.OBJ w/ no TU - investigate, record'). Records only, no edits; measured at 1a7f0393e.

WHAT THE BLUEPRINT SAID. claim.BE_the-enemy-gauntworld-blob-aliasing-is-not-aliasing-it-is-a-text-split-misassignment-inside-gamemain.20260904.v1 places GAMEDEFS.OBJ at default_options 0x800520CC and makes it the reason the enemy/gamemain boundary candidate 0x800522E8 'must be settled first', calling it 'either a mis-adopted name or an unsplit fourth TU'.

WHAT THE POOL SAYS, and it narrows the block. The per-function .sdata2 census over 0x80346700..0x80346D00 (every lbl_ symbol each function references in the dtk split asm) gives, in address order across the region: the ENEMY block ends at 0x80346AA4 (EnemyDescType); then 0x80346AB0 is read by game_main; then 0x80346AB8 is read by fn_800521E8; then 0x80346ABC.. is read by do_stats_display, and the real GAMEMAIN block runs on to 0x80346BD8 (init_thermometer). fn_800521E8's single pool entry therefore sits STRICTLY INSIDE the interval spanned by two functions that are unambiguously GAMEMAIN.OBJ's. Two objects' .sdata2 runs are concatenated by the linker and cannot interleave, so fn_800521E8 is GAMEMAIN.OBJ's, not GAMEDEFS.OBJ's -- the same interleave test that proved the gauntworld block and gauntworld.c are one object.

WHAT REMAINS UNDECIDED, honestly. default_options (0x800520CC, 0x68) and fn_80052134 (0x80052134, 0xB4) reference NO .rodata and NO .sdata2 datum at all (both read `-` in the census), and no .data label either, so the pool test is silent on them and only the PDB row and their .text position speak. If GAMEDEFS.OBJ is a real fourth object here its .text is 0x800520CC..0x800521E8 (0x11C bytes, two functions) and the real GAMEMAIN.OBJ begins at fn_800521E8 0x800521E8, NOT at do_stats_display 0x800522E8 as the blueprint's candidate has it.

SUPPORTING DETAIL FROM THE PDB, which fits a GC-vs-Xbox divergence rather than a mis-adoption. Xbox GAMEDEFS.OBJ holds five functions and one datum: default_options (0x52, G), load_options (1, G), save_options (1, G), SetNumPlayers (0x5B, G), UpdateDoPrint (0x23, G), doprint (D). load_options and save_options are ONE BYTE each on Xbox -- bare `ret` stubs. The GC block has three functions of 0x68 / 0xB4 / 0x100, i.e. default_options plus two substantial bodies, and `grep -n 'doprint\|SetNumPlayers\|UpdateDoPrint' config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt` returns NOTHING -- none of those three names exists anywhere in the GC image's symbol map. So the GC build's options layer is not the Xbox one function for function, and a positional adoption of the two unnamed bodies would be guesswork.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PHASE-2 ENEMY MOVE, which is what this investigation was gating. The enemy/gamemain .text boundary moves from 0x80050054 up to 0x800520CC (fn_800520C8, the ENEMY block's last function, is 4 bytes and ends exactly there), and gamemain keeps 0x800520CC..0x80055CB8 -- i.e. gamemain absorbs the GAMEDEFS prefix, which is the STATUS QUO for those bytes and needs no decision. Splitting GAMEDEFS out is a separate, later act that requires a src/game/game/gamedefs.c to exist; there is none in the tree (`ls src/game/game` shows combat.c, controls.c, gamemain.c, player.c, pmotion.c). Recording it so the next lane does not re-derive the same narrowing: the block to carve, if anyone carves it, is 0x800520CC..0x800521E8 and not 0x800520CC..0x800522E8.
